summary: Sterile Water for Injection is nonpyrogenic, solute-free water used exclusively to dissolve or dilute other parenteral drugs. It is NOT a therapeutic agent and must NEVER be infused alone or undiluted - its entry into the circulation in solute-free form causes hemolysis. Once an appropriate solute (drug or electrolyte) is added, the resulting isotonic/near-isotonic admixture is administered by the route specified for that drug.
indications: Diluent/vehicle for reconstituting and diluting parenteral medications
Use with automated compounding devices for preparing intravenous admixtures (pharmacy bulk package)

dosage.d: Volume determined by the drug being reconstituted or diluted
dosage.n: Never used as a fixed therapeutic dose

dosage.d: Used with automated compounding devices to prepare IV admixtures

admin: FOR DILUTION ONLY - never infuse alone or undiluted
Solute-free water entering the circulation undiluted causes hemolysis
Add the appropriate drug/solute to achieve an approximately isotonic solution before administration
Use strict aseptic technique; prepare admixtures under a laminar flow hood
Do not heat over 66 C (150 F)
Inspect for clarity and absence of particulate matter before use
moa: Sterile Water for Injection has no pharmacologic action of its own. It serves as a chemically inert vehicle (H2O) to dissolve or dilute drugs. Because it contains no solute, direct intravascular administration would create a markedly hypotonic environment that lyses red blood cells (hemolysis); therefore it must be combined with an appropriate solute first.

absolute: Do not use undiluted/without an added solute (causes hemolysis)
Do not use the pharmacy bulk package for non-automated admixture preparation
relative: Caution when large admixture volumes are given to patients prone to fluid overload
monitor: Hemolysis if inadvertent undiluted administration is suspected

preg: Sterile Water itself poses no inherent risk in pregnancy; any risk relates to the medication being reconstituted or diluted with it.
lact: Sterile Water itself poses no inherent risk during lactation; consider the drug it is used to prepare.
renal: No adjustment is required for the diluent. However, large volumes of resulting admixtures can contribute to fluid/electrolyte disturbance in renal impairment - monitor accordingly.
hepatic: No adjustment is required for the diluent itself.

interactions.diagnostics: Excessive admixture volumes may dilute serum electrolyte concentrations

common: None when used correctly as a diluent
serious: Fluid and/or solute overload with large admixture volumes
rare: Febrile response, infection at injection site, venous thrombosis or phlebitis from preparation technique
emergency: Acute intravascular hemolysis from inadvertent undiluted infusion

monitoring: Serum electrolytes and osmolality with large-volume admixtures
Fluid balance and signs of overhydration
counsel: This is a diluent, not a treatment in itself
It is prepared and administered only by trained healthcare professionals
Report any sudden discomfort, dark urine, or breathing difficulty during infusion of admixtures
pk: Not applicable; water distributes/excreted per body water handling
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from freezing
pearls: NEVER infuse Sterile Water for Injection alone - undiluted solute-free water causes acute hemolysis
Always add an appropriate solute to render the admixture approximately isotonic before IV use
Distinct from Bacteriostatic Water (which contains benzyl alcohol) and from Sterile Water for Irrigation (not for injection)
pH is about 5.4 (range 5.0-7.0); contains no antimicrobial preservative or buffer
missed: Not applicable - Sterile Water for Injection is a diluent, not a scheduled therapeutic dose.
overdose: Inadvertent undiluted intravascular administration causes hemolysis; large admixture volumes can cause fluid/solute overload, dilutional hyponatremia, overhydration, and pulmonary edema. Management is supportive: stop the infusion, correct electrolyte and fluid disturbances, and treat hemolysis as clinically indicated.
